feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 0 (the only raced design) gave zero completions: every trial ended off_track with max_error about 0.061 m and one line-loss event, so the robot lost the line early on every track. This is the basis for the widened seven-sensor array and the narrower 0.10 m track. The Integrator had to scale the sensor weights to the wider span (outer weights 1.5) so the signal stays monotonic, and to lower base_speed to 1.4 and raise kp to 3.0 to give the controller more correction per bend. The shorter lookahead at y = 0.04 m was chosen so kd does not add too much lag, which the iteration 0 feedback reported as hard to tune at y = 0.06 m. Decide the next geometry from what the next race shows. If line_loss_events is still above zero on the oval or S-bend, the sensor footprint is too small to bridge the gap, so try sensor_size 0.016 before changing the span again. If max_error still approaches 0.06 m with no line loss, the limit is being reached through controller lag, not sensor coverage, so reduce mass or base_speed rather than widening body_width, which cannot move the limit above 0.06 m. If runs complete but completion_time exceeds 2.5 s, increase top speed by moving to wheel_radius 0.035 m.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events stays above zero on the oval or S-bend with seven sensors, test sensor_size 0.016 at the same x = -0.03 to +0.03 m positions, since iteration 0 showed the 12 mm footprint loses the tape at moderate offsets.

If max_error still approaches 0.06 m with no line loss, reduce mass to 0.6 kg rather than widening body_width, because iteration 0 showed body_width cannot raise the 0.06 m off-track limit and the failure is from lag.
If runs complete but completion_time exceeds 2.5 s, test wheel_radius 0.035 m for more top speed, because iteration 0 had no completions to show the speed headroom.
